name: Magdiel
overview: Magdiel was a male Edomite chief mentioned in the book of Genesis. As a leader within the Edomite tribe, he held a position of authority among the descendants of Esau. The biblical record provides limited information beyond his role as a chief.
namesAndTitles: The name Magdiel means "choice gift of G-d [El]," reflecting a name of significance though it was not explicitly given by God. This proper name underscores a recognition of divine blessing or favor associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Magdiel as a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. Beyond this connection, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Magdiel's importance lies in his status as a chief of Edom, representing the organized tribal leadership among Esau's descendants. His mention in Genesis 36:43 highlights the established governance within Edom, which is significant for understanding the historical and genealogical context of the Edomite people in Scripture.
